author: Shaquira Speaks
title: 'Education is not being treated as a priority': Parents voice concerns on Gaston County Schools budget shortfalls - NewsBreak
text:
By Shaquira Speaks ,
43 minutes ago
GASTON COUNTY, N.C. ( QUEEN CITY NEWS ) — Gaston County commissioners approved the county schools’ new budget, giving them just over $35 million. But that’s just over half of the money district leaders say they need.
“Education is not being treated as a priority, and our kids are being told to go without,” said parent Samantha Easters. “They sat in that meeting, and they talked about how inflation is causing things to go up and the loss of funding with COVID funds, etc. And stated that the schools were just expected to absorb inflation when they were expected to do more with less, less and less.”
PREVIOUS: Gaston County commissioners approve budget, requests review of school district’s revenue She was one of dozens who spoke to county commissioners Tuesday, expressing their concerns about the budget movement ahead.
She suggested that commissioners look for other ways to fund teachers and staff, such as cutting jobs in local government.
Commissioner Jim Bailey agreed. He was the only dissenting vote on the budget.
“I compared ourselves to four other counties in Gaston County, that have a similar makeup and everything. Gaston County spends approximately 19% on the schools, and the other four average 33.5%. I would like to direct the county manager to reduce the size of our government,” Bailey said.
The district already plans to eliminate 174 positions ahead of the next school year, despite emergency funding from the county. More layoffs are likely if no additional funding is provided.
Superintendent Morgen Houchard says it needs the money for more than just teacher salaries.
“It’s those services that local dollars help support because we do everything in schools, we get them there, we feed them, we do their laundry for some students, we brush their teeth, we worry about their social-emotional well-being. And then we got to do ABCs and 123s, and we take them as athletic events. We do everything for them, and there’s a cost for that. A flat budget is not what’s best,” Houchard said.
“I’m not just thinking about my daughter, I’m thinking about the community. And in order to have a stable future in Gaston County, you have to prioritize education. And I want to see Gaston County grow,” Easters said.
Commissioners will set up meetings with district leaders in the next few weeks to determine the next steps, including sustainable staffing over the next few years. The board of education will hold a special personnel meeting on Thursday at 1 p.m.
The budget goes into effect on July 1.
